RTC timer is a real-time counter (using RTC slow clock) that can be configured to log the time when one of the following events happens.

blocks.caption: Table 10.3-2. The Triggering Conditions for the RTC Timer

c.v: RTC main state machine powers down or
CPU enters or exits the stall state. This is to ensure the SYS_TIMER is continuous in time.
The RTC timer updates two groups of registers upon any new trigger.
The first group logs the time of the current trigger, and the other logs the previous trigger.
Detailed information about these two register groups is shown below:
Register group 0: logs the status of RTC timer at the current trigger.
Register group 1: logs the status of RTC timer at the previous trigger.

On a new trigger, information on previous trigger is moved from register group 0 to register group 1 (and the original trigger logged in register group 1 is overwritten), and this new trigger is logged in register group 0.
Therefore, only the last two triggers can be logged at any time.
It should be noted that any reset/sleep other than power-up reset will not stop or reset the RTC timer.
Also, the RTC timer can be used as a wakeup source.
